clauses.clause: Single paragraph, part 1: the described Arizona tract (110-111 deg. W, 35 deg. 30 min.-36 deg. 30 min. N) is withdrawn from settlement and sale
Single paragraph, part 2: the tract is set apart for the use and occupancy of the Moqui (Hopi)
Single paragraph, part 3: also set apart for such other Indians as the Secretary of the Interior may see fit to settle there

moves.note: Transcription found at American Presidency Project, signed Chester A. Arthur, citing Kappler (GPO 1904) p. 805. Pub. L. 85-547 officially calls it an Executive order.
Kappler vol. 1 p. 805 not opened (okstate certificate error, 404 on alternate URL); LOC catalogue page returned 403. Clause list below is drawn from the transcription only.
Provisional status OPEN. No ending found; 1958 Act continues the land in trust by name. Current source found is descriptive and dated before the cutoff.

propositions.claim: The order, dated 16 December 1882 and signed by Chester A. Arthur, withdraws a described Arizona tract from settlement and sale (transcription).
propositions.quote: It is hereby ordered that the tract of country in the Territory of Arizona [...] be, and the same is hereby, withdrawn from settlement and sale,

propositions.claim: The tract begins on the 110th meridian at 36 deg. 30 min. north and runs west to the 111th meridian (transcription).
propositions.quote: beginning on the one hundred and tenth degree of longitude west from Greenwich, at a point 36 degrees and 30 minutes north,

propositions.claim: The tract is set apart for the Moqui and for other Indians the Secretary of the Interior chooses to settle there (transcription).
propositions.quote: and set apart for the use and occupancy of the Moqui and such other Indians as the Secretary of the Interior may see fit to settle thereon.

propositions.claim: Pub. L. 85-547 (22 July 1958) names the order as an Executive order and declares its lands held in trust for the Hopi and for other Indians already settled there by the Secretary; it does not revoke the order.
propositions.quote: lands described in the Executive order dated December 16, 1882, are hereby declared to be held by the United States in trust for the Hopi Indians and such other Indians, if any,

propositions.claim: Section 2 of the 1958 Act makes lands found to be exclusively Navaho part of the Navaho Indian Reservation.
propositions.quote: determined by the court to have the exclusive interest shall thereafter be a part of the Navaho Indian Reservation.

propositions.claim: Section 2 of the 1958 Act makes lands found to be exclusively Hopi a reservation for the Hopi Indian Tribe.
propositions.quote: are determined by the court to have the exclusive interest shall thereafter be a reservation for the Hopi Indian Tribe.

propositions.claim: The CFR edition revised 1 April 2025 (25 CFR 168.1(f)) still defines the Former Joint Use Area by reference to the order's area.
propositions.quote: inside the Executive order area (Executive order of December 16, 1882) but outside Land Management District 6

propositions.claim: The same CFR section treats part of the former Joint Use Area as added to the Hopi reservation.
propositions.quote: means that portion of the Former Joint Use Area which has been added to the Hopi Tribe's reservation.

propositions.claim: A 1996 Senate report states that Healing v. Jones gave the Hopi Tribe exclusive rights in District Six.
propositions.quote: the court held that the Hopi Tribe had the exclusive right to lands in District Six

propositions.claim: The same Senate report states that the Joint Use Area was partitioned in 1979.
propositions.quote: The Joint Use Area was finally partitioned in 1979

propositions.claim: 25 U.S.C. 640d (Pub. L. 93-531, sec. 1, the 1974 Settlement Act) is now omitted from the Code, so the Code gives no current note treating the order as in force there.
propositions.quote: omitted from the Code as being of special and not general application.

review.conclusion_reason: OPEN follows because the verified sources establish neither an express ending nor affirmative operation at the cutoff. The geographic CFR reference alone does not establish continuing legal force. Formal status is supportable only as no express ending found in the reviewed evidence, not proof that none exists. The accepted-original and clause-status gaps remain.
review.stop_code_verdict: confirmed — WEB fits the first gap: the evidence slice identifies Kappler volume I, page 805 as an external original-source lead and supplies no held-file location. The cited APP text remains a transcription; the evidence slice does not establish an available accepted original.

verdicts.reason: APP displays the stated date, Arthur's signature, and withdrawal language; correctly identified as a transcription.
APP's full paragraph confirms the starting coordinates and westward boundary to the 111th meridian.
APP reproduces the stated Moqui occupancy provision and Secretary's discretion concerning other Indians.
72 Stat. 403, section 1, names the order and declares the trust for Hopi and Indians previously settled under it. The complete Act contains no express revocation.
Section 2 expressly provides the stated conditional incorporation into the Navaho reservation.
Section 2 expressly provides the stated conditional establishment of a Hopi reservation.

The XML could not be fetched, but the identical official 2025 CFR PDF, pages 665–666, confirms section 168.1(f), its geographic reference, and the April 1, 2025 edition date: https://www.govinfo.gov/content/pkg/CFR-2025-title25-vol1/pdf/CFR-2025-title25-vol1-sec168-1.pdf
The official PDF equivalent confirms this definition in section 168.1(g), page 666.
Senate Report 104-363, background discussion of Healing v. Jones, expressly states the exclusive District Six rights.
The report's historical discussion expressly dates final partition to 1979 and describes allocations to both tribes.

Cornell's codification note confirms omission for special rather than general application. This section's displayed notes provide no affirmative continuation of the order; omission does not establish its termination.
